 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE A.Y. KOGJE  Date : 21/12/2020

This application under Section 378(1)(3) of Code of Criminal Procedure seeking leave to appeal against the judgment and order dated 31.12.2019 passed in Criminal Case No.516 of 1996 by the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Rajkot at Gondal, whereby recorded acquittal of the respondent in connection with the offence under Section 7(5) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.

entities.text: Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Rajkot at Gondal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Learned APP, at the outset, points out that the impugned judgment is devoid of any reasoning and narration of only cited judgments are made.
In so far as reasoning are concerned, the entire judgment consist of only one paragraph of reasoning and that too a reasoning which can be termed to be a perverse reasoning.

The acquittal based only on the ground that the samples of the turmeric powder was stored in a wooden box, and thereby, there was breach of mandatory provision of Rule 14 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules.

Learned APP draws attention of this Court by reading out deposition of the Food Inspector which indicate that the samples of turmeric powder was stored in dry transparent glass bottles and such glass bottles were appropriately sealed under the hands of the Food Inspector himself.
This disregarded R/CR.MA/18747/2020 ORDER by the Trial Court while recording the acquittal on sole ground.
